title: The Forest Reserve
story: You and NOVA are on a field trip to a biosphere reserve when the gate locks behind you. The ranger's computer opens it only when NOVA's forest knowledge is fixed.
escaped: The gate opens. NOVA now separates human and natural causes, knows flora from fauna and can scale a pattern.

locks.title: Flora or fauna?
locks.intro: NOVA is labelling what it sees in the reserve as flora (plants) or fauna (animals). Tick the wrong labels.

rows.label: Fauna
rows.why: a mango tree is a plant: flora

rows.label: Flora
rows.why: a leopard is an animal: fauna

locks.hint: Flora means plants; fauna means animals.
locks.learn: Even simple labels go wrong when people label in a hurry. A few wrong labels teach an AI muddled ideas, so people double-check training data.

locks.title: Human or natural cause?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort causes of forest loss into human causes and natural causes. Choose its clues.

train.name: Forest fire from a lightning strike

test.name: Cutting trees for furniture by hand
A forest fire from lightning in the rainy season

locks.hint: Not every human cause uses machines, and not every natural cause happens in summer.
locks.learn: Clues that happen to go along with a group in the examples (summer, machines) break on new cases. The clue that defines the groups, whether people did it, keeps working.

locks.title: Check NOVA's climate claim
locks.intro: NOVA explains what cutting forests does to the air. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: Cutting down forests lowers the carbon dioxide in the air.
evidence: Plants use carbon dioxide for photosynthesis, so with fewer trees less carbon dioxide is used up and more stays in the air.
Forests are home to many animals.
locks.hint: What do trees do with carbon dioxide?
locks.learn: AI can get cause and effect backwards. Checking how the process works (photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide) shows which way the effect goes.

locks.title: Trees saved by recycling
locks.intro: The textbook says about 17 full-grown trees are needed to make one tonne of paper. NOVA made a table.
locks.question: Your school recycles 5 tonnes of paper this year. About how many trees does that save?
locks.hint: Each tonne saves about 17 trees. Multiply.
locks.learn: Spotting a steady pattern (17 more trees for every tonne) lets an AI, or you, estimate new cases.
